text:
sam: Quick Q — gating a terraform change that adds multiplexed TLS ports on inference-gateway for a customer. We're adding 8443 alongside 443 and need healthchecks on 10256 to continue. Anyone seen Gateway API TCPRoute/TLSRoute + k8s svc healthcheck get forwarded to wrong backend with NLB passthrough? PR: https://git.redwood/example/pull/321
ali: Is this NLB passthrough or ALB termination? behaviour differs a lot. :thinking:
sam: NLB passthrough, targetType=ip, nodeport svc. goal: SNI on 443/8443 map to different backends, but healthprobe stays on 10256 plain TCP. wondering if svc port mapping or controller rewrites can break the probe
jess: We hit this before — kube-proxy + hostPort made the probe reach the pod but TLS handshake on probe port produced 502s. Workaround: expose a plain TCP readiness on 10256 and set externalTrafficPolicy: Local so healthchecks go to healthy pods only. Also set NLB annotations to point healthcheck at 10256
maria: Can you paste the TF/service snippet you're planning to apply?
sam: sure, here's the service piece in TF:
```
resource "kubernetes_service" "inference_gateway" {
  metadata {
    name = "inference-gateway"
    annotations = {
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type" = "nlb"
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type" = "ip"
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port" = "10256"
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol" = "TCP"
    }
  }
  spec {
    type = "NodePort"
    port {
      port        = 443
      target_port = 8443
    }
    port {
      port        = 8443
      target_port = 9443
    }
    port {
      port        = 10256
      target_port = 10256
    }
    selector = { app = "inference-gw" }
  }
}
```
ali: Also double-check aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol and externalTrafficPolicy. If you want client IP preserved and probe routing consistent, externalTrafficPolicy: Local helps but reduces spread
jess: and for NLB passthrough use TCPSocket readinessProbe in the pod (do NOT use HTTP probe unless TLS is terminated at LB). Example inside container:
```
readinessProbe:
  tcpSocket:
    port: 10256
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 10
```
devops-bot: PR 321: terraform plan passed in staging -> creating canary service inference-gateway-canary-1 :rocket:
sam: ok i'll update the pod probe to tcp and add the annotations. will also set externalTrafficPolicy: Local for the canary. pinging @eng-sre if they want to watch
maria: small nit — add `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type = "ip"` (you have it but ensure TF doesn't stomp it with defaults), and `aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port` must be a string not number in annotations
ali: +1 lmk when canary is up :thumbsup:
sam: updated PR -> https://git.redwood/example/pull/321/files — switched to TCPSocket readiness, externalTrafficPolicy: Local, and explicit healthcheck annotations. kicking off canary now
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for inference-gateway (canary-1) — watching health checks
jess: :eyes: i'll watch logs from staging and flag any 502/connection reset spikes
sam: if we still see TLS handshake on the probe, fallback plan is to move healthcheck to a separate mgmt port behind a plain TCP listener (eg 15020) and point the annotations there
ali: nice, thanks. spare note: record this in the infra-runbook for gateway TLS multiplexing edge cases
sam: will add a short note after canary completes
